160: export interface AnswerSelection {
161:   optionId: string | null;
162:   text: string;
163:   tokenIds: string[];
164: }
165: 
166: export interface LessonPlayerState {
167:   attemptId: string | null;
168:   isStarting: boolean;
169:   startError: string | null;
170:   currentIndex: number;
171:   isSubmitting: boolean;
172:   submitError: string | null;
173:   feedback: AnswerFeedback | null;
174:   isCompleted: boolean;
175:   selection: AnswerSelection;
176:   answers: boolean[];
177:   hearts: number | null;
178:   nextHeartAt: string | null;
179:   noHearts: boolean;
180: }
181: 
182: export type LessonPlayerAction =
183:   | { type: "START_REQUEST" }
184:   | { type: "START_SUCCESS"; attemptId: string }
185:   | { type: "START_FAILURE"; message: string }
186:   | { type: "SELECT_OPTION"; optionId: string }
187:   | { type: "SET_TEXT"; text: string }
188:   | { type: "TOGGLE_TOKEN"; tokenId: string }
189:   | { type: "SUBMIT_REQUEST" }
190:   | { type: "SUBMIT_SUCCESS"; feedback: AnswerFeedback }
191:   | { type: "SUBMIT_FAILURE"; message: string }
192:   | { type: "NO_HEARTS" }
193:   | { type: "UPDATE_HEARTS"; hearts: number; nextHeartAt: string | null }
194:   | { type: "NEXT" };
195: 
196: function emptySelection(): AnswerSelection {
197:   return { optionId: null, text: "", tokenIds: [] };
198: }
199: 
200: export const initialLessonPlayerState: LessonPlayerState = {
201:   attemptId: null,
202:   isStarting: false,
203:   startError: null,
204:   currentIndex: 0,
205:   isSubmitting: false,
206:   submitError: null,
207:   feedback: null,
208:   isCompleted: false,
209:   selection: emptySelection(),
210:   answers: [],
211:   hearts: null,
212:   nextHeartAt: null,
213:   noHearts: false,
214: };
215: 
216: export function lessonPlayerReducer(
217:   state: LessonPlayerState,
218:   action: LessonPlayerAction,
219: ): LessonPlayerState {
220:   switch (action.type) {
221:     case "START_REQUEST":
222:       // A second start while one is pending (or already started) is ignored.
223:       if (state.attemptId || state.isStarting) {
224:         return state;
225:       }
226:       return { ...state, isStarting: true, startError: null };
227: 
228:     case "START_SUCCESS":
229:       // Never replace an attempt that already exists.
230:       if (state.attemptId) {
231:         return state;
232:       }
233:       return {
234:         ...state,
235:         isStarting: false,
236:         attemptId: action.attemptId,
237:         startError: null,
238:       };
239: 
240:     case "START_FAILURE":
241:       return {
242:         ...state,
243:         isStarting: false,
244:         startError: action.message,
245:       };
246: 
247:     case "SELECT_OPTION":
248:       return {
249:         ...state,
250:         selection: { ...state.selection, optionId: action.optionId },
251:       };
252: 
253:     case "SET_TEXT":
254:       return {
255:         ...state,
256:         selection: { ...state.selection, text: action.text },
257:       };
258: 
259:     case "TOGGLE_TOKEN": {
260:       const isSelected = state.selection.tokenIds.includes(action.tokenId);
261:       const tokenIds = isSelected
262:         ? state.selection.tokenIds.filter(
263:             (tokenId) => tokenId !== action.tokenId,
264:           )
265:         : [...state.selection.tokenIds, action.tokenId];
266: 
267:       return {
268:         ...state,
269:         selection: { ...state.selection, tokenIds },
270:       };
271:     }
272: 
273:     case "SUBMIT_REQUEST":
274:       // Ignore a second submit while one is pending or once feedback exists.
275:       if (state.isSubmitting || state.feedback || state.isCompleted) {
276:         return state;
277:       }
278:       // Block submissions when no hearts remain.
279:       if (state.noHearts) {
280:         return state;
281:       }
282:       return { ...state, isSubmitting: true, submitError: null };
283: 
284:     case "SUBMIT_SUCCESS":
285:       // Ignore a response that no longer belongs to a pending submit.
286:       if (!state.isSubmitting) {
287:         return state;
288:       }
289:       return {
290:         ...state,
291:         isSubmitting: false,
292:         answers: [...state.answers, action.feedback.isCorrect],
293:         feedback: action.feedback,
294:         hearts: action.feedback.hearts ?? state.hearts ?? null,
295:         nextHeartAt: action.feedback.nextHeartAt ?? state.nextHeartAt ?? null,
296:         isCompleted: action.feedback.attempt.status === "COMPLETED",
297:       };
298: 
299:     case "SUBMIT_FAILURE":
300:       return {
301:         ...state,
302:         isSubmitting: false,
303:         submitError: action.message,
304:       };
305: 
306:     case "NO_HEARTS":
307:       return {
308:         ...state,
309:         noHearts: true,
310:         submitError:
311:           "No hearts remaining. Wait for a heart to regenerate before answering again.",
312:       };
313: 
314:     case "UPDATE_HEARTS":
315:       return {
316:         ...state,
317:         hearts: action.hearts,
318:         nextHeartAt: action.nextHeartAt,
319:       };
320: 
321:     case "NEXT":
322:       if (!state.feedback || state.isCompleted) {
323:         return state;
324:       }
325:       return {
326:         ...state,
327:         currentIndex: state.currentIndex + 1,
328:         feedback: null,
329:         submitError: null,
330:         selection: emptySelection(),
331:       };
332:   }
333: }
334: 
335: export function buildAnswerInput(
336:   exercise: LessonExercise,
337:   selection: AnswerSelection,
338: ): AnswerInput | null {
339:   switch (exercise.type) {
340:     case "MULTIPLE_CHOICE":
341:       return selection.optionId
342:         ? {
343:             type: "MULTIPLE_CHOICE",
344:             answer: { optionId: selection.optionId },
345:           }
346:         : null;
347: 
348:     case "FILL_BLANK": {
349:       const text = selection.text.trim();
350:       return text ? { type: "FILL_BLANK", answer: { text } } : null;
351:     }
352: 
353:     case "WORD_BANK":
354:       return selection.tokenIds.length > 0
355:         ? {
356:             type: "WORD_BANK",
357:             answer: { tokenIds: [...selection.tokenIds] },
358:           }
359:         : null;
360:   }
361: }
362: 
363: function getErrorMessage(error: unknown, fallback: string): string {
364:   return error instanceof Error && error.message ? error.message : fallback;
365: }

   - Create new attempt only if no existing attempt

- Client: TypeScript passes; some pre-existing test mock issues unrelated to these changes

```typescript
export async function startLessonAttemptAtomically(
  userId: string,
  lessonId: string,
  startedAt: Timestamp
): Promise<{ attempt: AttemptRecord; created: boolean }> {
  const db = getDb();
  const attemptDocRef = lessonAttemptDoc(userId, generateId());

  const result = await db.runTransaction(async (transaction) => {
    // Check for existing IN_PROGRESS attempt within the transaction
    const snapshot = await transaction.get(lessonAttemptsCol(userId));

    const existingAttempts = snapshot.docs
      .map(
        (doc): AttemptRecord => ({
          id: doc.id,
          ...LessonAttemptSchema.parse(doc.data()),
        })
      )
      .filter(
        (a): a is AttemptRecord => a.lessonId === lessonId && a.status === 'IN_PROGRESS'
      );

    if (existingAttempts.length > 0) {
      // Resume the most recent IN_PROGRESS attempt
      const attempt = existingAttempts.sort(
        (a, b) => b.startedAt.toMillis() - a.startedAt.toMillis()
      )[0];

      // Update the existing attempt to reset it for a fresh start
      transaction.update(lessonAttemptDoc(userId, attempt.id), {
        status: 'IN_PROGRESS',
        correctCount: 0,
        answeredCount: 0,
        startedAt,
      });

      return { attempt, created: false };
    }

    // No existing IN_PROGRESS attempt - create a new one
    const newAttempt: LessonAttempt = {
      lessonId,
      status: 'IN_PROGRESS',
      correctCount: 0,
      answeredCount: 0,
      totalExercises: 0,
      accuracy: null,
      xpAwarded: 0,
      startedAt,
    };

    transaction.set(attemptDocRef, newAttempt);

    return { attempt: newAttempt, created: true };
  });

  // The runTransaction returns the callback's return value
  return result as { attempt: AttemptRecord; created: boolean };
}
```

### Sprint 6.2 — AI-Powered Review Coach

Implement AI explanations for incorrectly answered exercises in the Home page Review Queue.

**Backend:**

1. Preserve the student's latest incorrect submitted answer in the existing review queue entry (`lastSubmittedAnswer`).
2. Extend the existing authenticated review queue data as needed.
3. Add authenticated `POST /api/ai/review-explanation`, accepting `{ exerciseId }`.
4. Verify the exercise exists in the authenticated user's review queue.
5. Fetch the original question, student's latest incorrect answer, correct answer and existing exercise explanation from Firestore.
6. Use the existing NVIDIA NIM configuration, API key and model. Reuse `ai.service.ts`; do not recreate the old conversation feature.
7. Ask AI to explain in simple English:
   - What the student answered.
   - What the correct answer is.
   - Why the student's answer was incorrect.
   - One helpful hint or example to remember it.
8. Treat the stored answer key as authoritative. AI must not invent or change the correct answer.
9. Return `{ explanation: string }`. Handle NIM failures safely without exposing credentials.

**Frontend:**

1. Keep the Review Queue exclusively on `LearningPathPage`.
2. Add an "Explain my mistake" action to each queued exercise.
3. On click, call the new explanation endpoint.
4. Display the AI explanation inside the corresponding queue card.
5. Add loading, error and retry states.
6. Do not introduce a separate Review page, chatbot, lesson replay or new navigation route.

**Allowed files only:**

Server:
1. `server/src/lib/schemas.ts`
2. `server/src/modules/learning/learning.repository.ts`
3. `server/src/modules/learning/learning.service.ts`
4. `server/src/modules/ai/ai.service.ts`
5. `server/src/modules/ai/ai.routes.ts`
6. `server/src/modules/ai/ai-review.test.ts` (new)

Client:
7. `client/src/features/learning-path/LearningPathPage.tsx`
8. `client/src/features/learning-path/LearningPathPage.test.tsx`

Inspect existing schemas and route registration read-only. Do not modify authentication, app routing, dependencies, seed data or other files. Ask permission if another file is essential.

**Important:** The existing `lesson-attempts.test.ts` has a previously reported corruption issue that we have deferred. Do not modify it during this sprint.

**Tests (Vitest):**
- Incorrect submission preserves the latest submitted answer.
- Repeated mistakes update the latest answer and wrongCount.
- First queued timestamp remains preserved.
- AI endpoint requires authentication.
- Exercises not belonging to the user's queue are rejected.
- Correct question, submitted answer and answer key reach the NIM prompt.
- AI explanation includes the correct answer and mistake explanation.
- NIM failures return safe errors.
- Home queue displays explanations and loading/error/retry states.
- Normal lesson APIs do not expose answer keys.

Mock all NVIDIA calls. No real API calls during tests.

**Validation:**
- Run only new/affected tests.
- Run targeted TypeScript checks if supported without touching the deferred corrupted test file.
- Do not run full suites or production builds.
- No new dependencies.

**Final output:** Exact files changed, API request/response example, implementation summary, tests, TypeScript results and limitations.

Do not modify chat history. Stop after Sprint 6.2.

### Sprint 6.2 — AI-Powered Review Coach

Implement AI explanations for incorrectly answered exercises in the Home page Review Queue.

**Backend:**

1. Preserve the student's latest incorrect submitted answer in the existing review queue entry (`lastSubmittedAnswer`).
2. Extend the existing authenticated review queue data as needed.
3. Add authenticated `POST /api/ai/review-explanation`, accepting `{ exerciseId }`.
4. Verify the exercise exists in the authenticated user's review queue.
5. Fetch the original question, student's latest incorrect answer, correct answer and existing exercise explanation from Firestore.
6. Use the existing NVIDIA NIM configuration, API key and model. Reuse `ai.service.ts`; do not recreate the old conversation feature.
7. Ask AI to explain in simple English:
   - What the student answered.
   - What the correct answer is.
   - Why the student's answer was incorrect.
   - One helpful hint or example to remember it.
8. Treat the stored answer key as authoritative. AI must not invent or change the correct answer.
9. Return `{ explanation: string }`. Handle NIM failures safely without exposing credentials.

**Frontend:**

1. Keep the Review Queue exclusively on `LearningPathPage`.
2. Add an "Explain my mistake" action to each queued exercise.
3. On click, call the new explanation endpoint.
4. Display the AI explanation inside the corresponding queue card.
5. Add loading, error and retry states.
6. Do not introduce a separate Review page, chatbot, lesson replay or new navigation route.

**Allowed files only:**

Server:

Client:

8. `client/src/features/learning-path/LearningPathPage.test.tsx`

**Important:** The existing `lesson-attempts.test.ts` has a previously reported corruption issue that we have deferred. Do not modify it during this sprint.

**Tests (Vitest):**
- Incorrect submission preserves the latest submitted answer.
- Repeated mistakes update the latest answer and wrongCount.
- First queued timestamp remains preserved.
- AI endpoint requires authentication.
- Exercises not belonging to the user's queue are rejected.
- Correct question, submitted answer and answer key reach the NIM prompt.
- AI explanation includes the correct answer and mistake explanation.
- NIM failures return safe errors.
- Home queue displays explanations and loading/error/retry states.
- Normal lesson APIs do not expose answer keys.

Mock all NVIDIA calls. No real API calls during tests.

**Validation:**
- Run only new/affected tests.
- Run targeted TypeScript checks if supported without touching the deferred corrupted test file.
- Do not run full suites or production builds.
- No new dependencies.

**Final output:** Exact files changed, API request/response example, implementation summary, tests, TypeScript results and limitations.

Do not modify chat history. Stop after Sprint 6.2.

function planReviewQueueAction(
  existing: ReviewItem | null,
  isCorrect: boolean,
  lessonId: string,
  exerciseId: string,
  submittedAt: Timestamp,
): ReviewQueueAction {
  if (isCorrect) {
    if (existing) {
      return { type: "DELETE" };
    }
    return { type: "NONE" };
  }

  if (existing) {
    return {
      type: "SET",
      entry: {
        lessonId,
        status: "PENDING",
        wrongCount: existing.wrongCount + 1,
        lastWrongAt: submittedAt,
        createdAt: existing.createdAt,
        updatedAt: submittedAt,
      },
    };
  }

  return {
    type: "SET",
    entry: {
      lessonId,
      status: "PENDING",
      wrongCount: 1,
      lastWrongAt: submittedAt,
      createdAt: submittedAt,
      updatedAt: submittedAt,
    },
  };
}

## Summary

**Sprint 6.3 complete** — Lessons 4–9 now seed into Firestore correctly.

### Root Cause
The JSON files for Lessons 4–9 had two classes of defects that blocked seeding:
1. **Malformed word bank entries** — `{ "id": "w2": "veux" }` instead of `{ "id": "w2", "text": "veux" }` across all 6 exercise files
2. **Unterminated prompt strings** — missing closing quotes in 8 prompts across lessons 5, 6, 7, 8, 9
3. **Duplicate exercise order** — Lesson 7 ex-7-5 had `order: 3` (same as ex-7-4)
4. **Answer-key/exercise mismatches** — broken FILL_BLANK prompts, incorrect WORD_BANK token references

### Fixes Applied
| File | Changes |
|------|---------|
| `server/src/scripts/seed.ts` | Added `seedLessonContent('lesson-4')` through `('lesson-9')` calls to `main()` |
| `exercises-lesson-4.json` | Fixed word bank JSON, corrected ex-4-3 prompt/accepted answer to `"Bonjour"` |
| `exercises-lesson-5.json` | Fixed word bank JSON, fixed ex-5-3 prompt/accepted/hint, fixed ex-5-6 prompt |
| `exercises-lesson-6.json` | Fixed word bank JSON, fixed ex-6-4 accepted/hint to `"à moitié"`, fixed ex-6-6 prompt |
| `exercises-lesson-7.json` | Fixed word bank JSON, fixed ex-7-5 order `3→4`, fixed ex-7-6 token to `"avez-vous"`, fixed ex-7-6 prompt |
| `exercises-lesson-8.json` | Fixed word bank JSON, fixed ex-8-3 accepted to `"un pain"`, fixed ex-8-4 prompt/accepted/hint, fixed ex-8-6 prompt |
| `exercises-lesson-9.json` | Fixed word bank JSON, fixed ex-9-3 prompt/accepted/hint to `"Tout droit"`, fixed ex-9-5/9-6 prompts |
| `answer-keys-lesson-4..9.json` | Updated all 6 files to match corrected exercises (FILL_BLANK accepted answers, WORD_BANK token IDs) |

### Verification Results
| Run | Learning Path | Units | Lessons | Exercises | Answer Keys |
|-----|---------------|-------|---------|-----------|-------------|
| 1 | 1 | 3 | 9 | 54 | 54 |
| 2 (idempotent) | 1 | 3 | 9 | 54 | 54 |
